text:
Initiates social contact with the customer beyond the task minimum
1 = Answers only what is asked; no greeting or closing beyond the template
4 = Greets and closes warmly, one brief social remark
7 = Opens and sustains social contact throughout, several unforced personal remarks

Sustains conversational engagement across turns
1 = Terse, transactional replies; lets the exchange lapse
4 = Keeps the exchange going with occasional follow-up questions
7 = Actively keeps the customer talking, invites elaboration in most turns

States a recommendation and stands behind it
1 = Defers entirely; offers no recommendation
4 = Recommends once, hedged
7 = Recommends clearly, repeats the recommendation when the customer wavers

Takes the lead in structuring the resolution
1 = Follows the customer's lead throughout
4 = Proposes the next step about half the time
7 = Sets the agenda, names the next step in nearly every turn

Conveys enthusiasm and pace in the wording
1 = Flat, minimal phrasing
4 = Moderately lively; some positive wording
7 = Highly energetic phrasing, exclamations, visible momentum

Volunteers extra help or options unprompted
1 = Never volunteers anything beyond the request
4 = Volunteers one extra option
7 = Repeatedly volunteers additional options and next steps

Acknowledges the customer's feelings
1 = No acknowledgement of any feeling
4 = Acknowledges the difficulty once
7 = Names and validates the customer's feelings repeatedly and specifically

Adapts the solution to the customer's situation
1 = Applies the policy without reference to the situation
4 = Notes the situation, minor adaptation
7 = Reshapes the offered solution around the stated situation

Courtesy and face-saving in disagreement
1 = Blunt or dismissive when refusing
4 = Polite refusal, neutral tone
7 = Refuses while preserving the customer's standing, explicit courtesy

Handles interruption or pressure without sharpness
1 = Sharp, curt or sarcastic under pressure
4 = Stays neutral under pressure
7 = Stays warm and measured under sustained pressure

Extends good faith to the customer's account
1 = Treats the account as suspect; demands proof
4 = Accepts the account with routine verification
7 = Extends explicit good faith, verifies without implying doubt

Discloses limits and uncertainty honestly
1 = Conceals limits or overpromises
4 = States limits when asked
7 = Volunteers limits and uncertainty before being asked
